- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish correction.  
- Model frequently over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; apply downward bias for days 1–5.  
- Model under-estimates late in horizon (days 25–30) when sentiment is neutral or positive; adjust upward for final 5–7 days.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; add slight resistance bias to prevent overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.25) and price is trending, model often misses the direction; use sentiment as a proxy for trend strength to adjust forecast slope.
